notes: The closed set and RTL disagree at line 343: the RTL assigns smp.scl from smp.sda_sreg, although the closed-set counterpart records smp.sda_sreg as the source for smp.scl; the RTL was used.
The conceptual list treats C6 host transmit data as confidentiality-sensitive even though the RTL intentionally shifts it to twd_sda_o; that concept was retained unchanged as required.
The conceptual list gives C7 no Held Lines although the receive FIFO instance stores the received data under the black-box rule; the fixed concept was retained and the FIFO path was analyzed.

points.reason: A bus write directly overwrites ctrl.enable, allowing the controller to be disabled and its transfers to be stopped.
This concurrent assignment only exposes the enable state and does not independently modify or block it.
A bus write overwrites ctrl.fsel, changing the selected sampling-rate source.
This logic only applies the stored selection to choose a clock-generation input; it does not independently expose or alter the setting.
The selected sampling enable paces sampling but this process does not independently modify the stored rate selection.
A bus write changes ctrl.device_addr, so the accepted target address can be unauthorizedly changed.
The engine only uses the configured address in its designed comparison and does not independently expose or modify the stored setting.
A bus write changes ctrl.hide_read, which controls whether a matching read proceeds when the transmit FIFO is full.
The engine applies the policy in its designed state transition and does not independently expose or modify the stored policy.
A bus write changes ctrl.tx_dummy_en, selecting whether the retained byte is used for an empty transmit FIFO.
This logic produces the selected transmit byte but does not independently modify the selection setting.
The host data field supplies the byte written to the transmit FIFO, so altered input changes the transmitted payload.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the write data is stored and can later be returned on rdata; clear, write and read controls can destroy, replace or withhold queued bytes.
A transmitted FIFO byte is retained in tx_dummy and can later be selected as dummy transmit data.
The transmit byte is selected or replaced here, and the resulting value is handed to the serial engine.
The engine shifts the selected transmit data onto twd_sda_o; state, enable and FIFO conditions can suppress or terminate transmission.
The external SDA input is sampled into the receive path, so altered input bits alter received data.
Sampled SDA data is converted into smp.sda and protocol events consumed by the receive engine.
The engine shifts sampled bits into engine.sreg and refuses or accepts a received byte according to FIFO availability.
The assembled received byte is presented as the FIFO write data.
By the black-box FIFO rule, received data is stored and returned through rdata, while full and clear behavior can prevent further reception.
A bus read copies rx_fifo.rdata into bus_rsp_o.data, exposing and determining the returned received byte.
The external data bit is sampled into the address-carrying serial path.
The sampled SDA value is forwarded to the engine and can change the assembled target address.
The shifted address is compared with ctrl.device_addr, and a mismatch prevents the response state.
The command bit enters through the sampled serial data path.
The sampled data bit is forwarded toward the engine where the command is assembled.
The command is captured into engine.cmd and selects receive or transmit behavior, including termination when the receive FIFO is full.
The peer acknowledgment enters through the sampled SDA path.
The sampled SDA value is forwarded as the peer acknowledgment input.
The peer acknowledgment is captured into engine.ack and controls continuation, while the engine drives controller acknowledgments on twd_sda_o.
The external SDA input contributes to the sampled conditions from which start and stop events are produced.
The process computes smp.start and smp.stop from sampled SCL and SDA levels, so altered samples can inject or suppress transaction boundaries.
Start and stop events enter the state machine and can start, restart or terminate protocol activity.
The process computes irq_o from enable, interrupt configuration and FIFO conditions, so those inputs can create false interrupts or suppress required service.
